# <a id="_4mpryxzk37i"></a>__The Great Balloon Embargo and the Poison Gift__

[JANET RILEY](https://substack.com/@juanita4141)

Jan 19, 2026

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

In our family, we don’t just celebrate birthdays; we weaponize them\. My sister has always operated under the firm belief that there are only two ways to do things: her way and the wrong way\. I, being the more flexible sibling, have always maintained that there’s a third way—a way that usually involves a long\-game prank\.

The “Cold War” peaked on my 60th birthday\. At the time, I worked in a massive office building with over 1,500 people\. On that particular morning, the lobby was packed for a community blood drive\. There were at least seven or eight hundred people milling about when a delivery man walked in clutching a massive, bobbing cloud of twenty black balloons\.

“Where’s Janet Riley?” he shouted\.

He delivered them right there, in the middle of the crowd\. I became the instant centerpiece of the “Over the Hill” club in front of half the building\. To make matters worse, I had to get those balloons up to my office on the fifth floor\. I didn’t just ride the elevator; I *was* the elevator\. There wasn’t room for a single other soul—just me and my twenty reminders of mortality drifting against the ceiling\. By the time I tied them to my desk, I had already begun to scheme\.

I waited\. I planned\. I knew that because we sat on opposite sides of the political aisle, I had a secret weapon\.

A few years later, at her birthday celebration, I handed her a carefully wrapped gag gift\. It was a piece of political memorabilia from “the other side”—something so contrary to her beliefs that I knew she wouldn’t even want it touching her carpet\.

The reaction was exactly what I’d rehearsed in my head\. She didn’t just open it; she recoiled\. She held it out at arm’s length, as if it were a literal piece of poison, and handed it right back to me before she even looked at her “nice” gift\.

“That,” I said with a smile, “is for the balloons\.”

I finally gave her the real present, but the true gift was the look on her face\. The scales were balanced, the elevator was empty, and the “Third Way” had won the day\.
